pairs.evidence: src/lib/server/json-file-store.ts:36 The corrupt-JSON refusal arm exists to stop data loss, but no test runs it: a grep of all *.test.ts and *.spec.ts files for readJsonFile, updateJsonFile, withWriteLock, json-file-store and fileLock finds nothing, so a refactor back to the empty fallback would stay green.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/server/json-file-store.ts:36 A recovery/refusal arm that the normal suite never runs. It has no test at all, so it has no negative control. The temp-file cleanup arm at line 65 is in the same position.
src/lib/server/rate-limit.test.ts:64 The window-refill and Retry-After claims run on a fake clock (advanceTimersByTime), not on wall time.
src/lib/server/rate-limit.test.ts:18 Bucket state is module-level, so each test gets a unique namespace instead of inheriting buckets from earlier tests. The test states this explicitly.

src/lib/server/rate-limit.test.ts:11 The rate-limit tests assert the admit/refuse direction, so the limiter's decision is actually reached and the assertion depends on it. The comment names the inversion mutation the tests defend against.
